lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Mini: Why blank chart ≠ empty land; name one respectful source habit for First Nations content.

FEEDBACK
People already lived there; use published/Community sources and do not invent sacred knowledge.

WATCH FOR
A showcase of explorer heroes with no First Nations presence repeats erasure.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Assemble a showcase checklist: five key ideas, each with a source or “needs Community verification” tag. Practise a one-minute talk that includes First Nations presence before 1788.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Assemble a showcase checklist: five key ideas, each with a source or “needs Community verification” tag. Practise a one-minute talk that includes First Nations presence before 1788. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: People already lived there; use published/Community sources and do not invent sacred knowledge. Reasoning: I used review by attending to showcase rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: A showcase of explorer heroes with no First Nations presence repeats erasure. Correction: People already lived there; use published/Community sources and do not invent sacred knowledge. Why: the correction restores accurate use of review.

Parent: Likely misconception: A showcase of explorer heroes with no First Nations presence repeats erasure. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating review on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with review, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.
